name: Cyber-Mage
description: Master programmers and spell casters who encode complex spell subroutines into cyberdecks, optical arrays, and neural focuses.

choices.selection_effect: Record proficiency in the selected skills.

multiclass_proficiencies.description: Gain the Hit Point Die from the Core Wizard Traits table.

starting_equipment.description: Choose A or B: (A) 2 Daggers, Arcane Focus (Quarterstaff), Robe, Spellbook, Scholar’s Pack, and 5 GP; or (B) 55 GP Starting equipment is not granted on multiclass entry.

spellcasting.preparation_rule: Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.
spellcasting.ritual_casting_rule: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn’t have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.
spellcasting.focus_rule: Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.
spellcasting.multiclass_slot_rule: Full caster; verify shared multiclass slot calculation under the chosen edition.
spellcasting.notes: See the level 1 Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature for casting, preparation, focus, and replacement rules. Null fields require review; the reference spell mapping may not be a complete 2024 spell list.

resources.name: RAM Defrag & Buffer Flush
resources.description:
See the Arcane Recovery feature for costs, use, and recovery. You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you’re a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels’ worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.

Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
resources.maximum_rule: See the feature and level table; resolve structured maximum and recovery rules before implementation.

features.name: Spellcasting: Digital Architecture & Executable Modules (Spellcasting)
features.description:
As a student of arcane magic, you have learned to cast spells. See “Spells” for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Wizard spells, which appear in the Wizard spell list later in the class’s description.

Cantrips. You know three Wizard cantrips of your choice. Light, Mage Hand, and Ray of Frost are recommended. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips from this feature with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

When you reach Wizard levels 4 and 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Wizard Features table.

Spellbook. Your wizardly apprenticeship culminated in the creation of a unique book: your spellbook. It is a Tiny object that weighs 3 pounds, contains 100 pages, and can be read only by you or someone casting Identify. You determine the book’s appearance and materials, such as a gilt-edged tome or a collection of vellum bound with twine.

The book contains the level 1+ spells you know. It starts with six level 1 Wizard spells of your choice. Detect Magic, Feather Fall, Mage Armor, Magic Missile, Sleep, and Thunderwave are recommended.

Whenever you gain a Wizard level after 1, add two Wizard spells of your choice to your spellbook. Each of these spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots, as shown in the Wizard Features table. The spells are the culmination of arcane research you do regularly.

Spell Slots. The Wizard Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

Prepared Spells of Level 1+. You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To do so, choose four spells from your spellbook. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Wizard levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Wizard Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you’re a level 3 Wizard, your list of prepared spells can include six spells of levels 1 and 2 in any combination, chosen from your spellbook.

If another Wizard feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don’t count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Wizard spells for you.

Changing Your Prepared Spells. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with spells from your spellbook.

Spellcasting Ability. Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

Spellcasting Focus. You can use an Arcane Focus or your spellbook as a Spellcasting Focus for your Wizard spells.

Expanding and Replacing a Spellbook

The spells you add to your spellbook as you gain levels reflect your ongoing magical research, but you might find other spells during your adventures that you can add to the book. You could discover a Wizard spell on a Spell Scroll, for example, and then copy it into your spellbook.

Copying a Spell into the Book. When you find a level 1+ Wizard spell, you can copy it into your spellbook if it’s of a level you can prepare and if you have time to copy it. For each level of the spell, the transcription takes 2 hours and costs 50 GP. Afterward you can prepare the spell like the other spells in your spellbook.

Copying the Book. You can copy a spell from your spellbook into another book. This is like copying a new spell into your spellbook but faster, since you already know how to cast the spell. You need spend only 1 hour and 10 GP for each level of the copied spell.

If you lose your spellbook, you can use the same procedure to transcribe the Wizard spells that you have prepared into a new spellbook. Filling out the remainder of the new book requires you to find new spells to do so. For this reason, many wizards keep a backup spellbook.

reskin_reference.name: 2. Spellcasting: Digital Architecture & Executable Modules (Level 1)
reskin_reference.description: As a practitioner of Matrix code manipulation and digital sorcery, you operate a customized Cyberdeck containing compiled code modules and daemon scripts.

features.name: Low-Bandwidth Utilities (Cantrips)
features.description: At 1st level, you know three low-bandwidth utility scripts of your choice from the Cyber-Mage module list. These micro-programs require minimal clock cycles and are permanently cached in your active RAM for instant execution without expending deck power cells. You learn additional utility scripts at higher levels (4 at 4th level, 5 at 10th level).

features.name: Cyberdeck / Neural Memory Matrix (Spellbook)
features.description: At 1st level, you possess a Cyberdeck pre-loaded with six 1st-level executable code modules of your choice. Your Cyberdeck is the secure repository of all complex programs you know, excluding your cached utilities. The code modules you add as you gain levels reflect your independent signal research, dark-web data digs, and system breakthroughs.

features.name: Caching & Program Allocation (Preparing and Casting Spells)
features.description: The Cyber-Mage table shows how many Deck Power Cells (spell slots) you have to launch programs of 1st level and higher. To run a compiled program, you must consume a Deck Power Cell of that program's level or higher. You fully recharge all depleted power cells when you finish a System Power Cycle (Long Rest). You mount a curated list of programs into active RAM equal to your Intelligence modifier + your Cyber-Mage level (minimum 1). Re-mounting a new list requires spending 1 minute per program level after a System Power Cycle.

features.name: Primary Processing Ability: System Architecture (Spellcasting Ability)
features.description: Intelligence is your primary System Architecture ability for Cyber-Mage programs, as your digital sorcery relies on advanced logic, network topology, and code execution. Program Firewall Save DC = 8 + Proficiency Bonus + Intelligence modifier. Program Attack Modifier = Proficiency Bonus + Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Background Daemon Execution (Ritual Casting)
features.description: You can launch a program as an Offline Background Daemon if that module carries the [Daemon] tag and is compiled within your Cyberdeck. You do not need to mount the program into active RAM, but launching a daemon adds 10 extra minutes of system compile time.

features.name: Interface Focus (Spellcasting Focus)
features.description: You can use a specialized Hardware Focus—such as a neural interface wrist-rig, a high-frequency signal wand, a sub-dermal coprocessor, or your Cyberdeck chassis—as a system focus for executing your programs.

features.name: Compiling Code & System Backups (Copying Spells & Replacement)
features.description: When you find a Cyber-Mage program of 1st level or higher, you can compile it into your Cyberdeck if you can process its level. For each level of the program, the process takes 2 hours and costs 50 credits (gp) for diagnostic solder, thermal paste, and decryption licenses. Duplicating your own programs to a backup drive requires 1 hour and 10 credits per program level.

features.name: Ritual Adept
features.description: You can cast any spell as a Ritual if that spell has the Ritual tag and the spell is in your spellbook. You needn’t have the spell prepared, but you must read from the book to cast a spell in this way.

features.name: RAM Defrag & Buffer Flush (Arcane Recovery)
features.description:
You can regain some of your magical energy by studying your spellbook. When you finish a Short Rest, you can choose expended spell slots to recover. The spell slots can have a combined level equal to no more than half your Wizard level (round up), and none of the slots can be level 6 or higher. For example, if you’re a level 4 Wizard, you can recover up to two levels’ worth of spell slots, regaining either one level 2 spell slot or two level 1 spell slots.

Once you use this feature, you can’t do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

reskin_reference.name: 3. RAM Defrag & Buffer Flush (Arcane Recovery) (Level 1)
reskin_reference.description: You have learned to purge temporary cache files and clear thermal throttling during a Quick Diagnostic Pause.

features.name: Mechanics
features.description: Once per day when you finish a Quick Diagnostic Pause (Short Rest), you can execute an automated RAM defragmentation cycle to recover depleted Deck Power Cells. The recovered power cells can have a combined level equal to or less than half your Cyber-Mage level (rounded up), and none of the recovered cells can be 6th level or higher.

features.name: Permanent Neural Kernel Caching (Spell Mastery)
features.description:
You have achieved such mastery over certain spells that you can cast them at will. Choose a level 1 and a level 2 spell in your spellbook that have a casting time of an action. You always have those spells prepared, and you can cast them at their lowest level without expending a spell slot. To cast either spell at a higher level, you must expend a spell slot.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can study your spellbook and replace one of those spells with an eligible spell of the same level from the book.

subclasses.name: Neon Bladesinger
subclasses.description: A spellblade who combines precise weapon work with a cybernetically enhanced arcane combat rhythm. Reskin of the supplied Bladesinger.

resources.name: Neon Combat Rhythm
resources.description: Each activation of Neon Combat Rhythm expends one use.
resources.maximum_rule: Intelligence modifier, minimum 1; regain all expended uses on a long rest.

features.name: Neon Combat Rhythm (Bladesong)
features.description: As a bonus action, activate the rhythm if you wear no armor and use no shield. It lasts 1 minute; it ends early if you are incapacitated, put on armor or a shield, or make a weapon attack using two hands. You can dismiss it at any time without an action. While active, add your Intelligence modifier to AC (minimum +1), increase your speed by 10 feet, and add your Intelligence modifier to Constitution saving throws to maintain concentration. When attacking with a weapon you are proficient with, you can use Intelligence instead of Strength or Dexterity for both attack and damage rolls. Uses equal your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1), restored on a long rest.

features.name: Street Combat Training (Training in War and Song)
features.description: Gain proficiency with all martial melee weapons without the Heavy or Two-Handed property. You can use a melee weapon you are proficient with as a spellcasting focus for your Cyber-Mage spells. Gain proficiency in one listed skill.

choices.name: Choose a combat training skill
choices.eligibility_rule: Choose one listed skill; the supplied source does not specify a replacement for an already-proficient skill.
choices.selection_effect: Record proficiency in the selected skill.

features.name: Spellblade Weave (Extra Attack)
features.description: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can attack twice instead of once. You can replace one of those attacks with a Cyber-Mage cantrip that has a casting time of an action.

features.name: Defensive Feedback (Song of Defense)
features.description: When you take damage while Neon Combat Rhythm is active, use a reaction and expend a spell slot to reduce that damage by five times the slot's level.

features.name: Finishing Sequence (Song of Victory)
features.description: After casting a spell with a casting time of an action, you can make one weapon attack as a bonus action.

subclasses.name: System Forensics Diviner
subclasses.description: A predictive analyst who extracts arcane intelligence from signals and possible futures. Reskin of the supplied Diviner.

resources.name: Predictive Algorithm Matrix
resources.description: Roll and record the foretelling d20s after a long rest; each recorded result can replace one eligible D20 Test. Discard unused results at the next long rest.
resources.maximum_rule: Two recorded rolls at class level 3; three instead at class level 14. Roll new results after each long rest.

resources.name: Full Spectrum Threat Scan
resources.description: Activate one sensory benefit; it lasts until you start a short or long rest.
resources.maximum_rule: One use beginning at class level 10; regain it after a short or long rest.

features.name: Analysis Compiler Savant (Divination Savant)
features.description: Add two eligible Divination Wizard spells of level 1 or 2 to your spellbook for free. Whenever you gain access to a new spell-slot level in this class, add one eligible Divination Wizard spell of a level for which you have spell slots to your spellbook for free. These additions are in addition to the normal class spellbook selections.

choices.name: Choose two Divination spells for the spellbook
choices.allowed_options: Level 1 or 2 Wizard spells of the Divination school.
choices.eligibility_rule: Choose two distinct eligible spells not already in your spellbook.
choices.selection_effect: Add both spells to the spellbook for free; these are not automatically prepared.

features.name: Predictive Algorithm Matrix (Portent)
features.description: After a long rest, roll two d20s and record the results. Before a D20 Test by you or a creature you can see is rolled, you can replace that roll with one recorded result, at most once per turn. Each result is used once; discard unused results when you finish a long rest. At Cyber-Mage level 14, roll three d20s instead.

levels.notes: The initial Savant grant includes spells of level 2. The supplied source does not resolve whether gaining the feature at the same level as level 2 slots also triggers an additional Savant spell; review before automation.

features.description: Add two eligible Necromancy Wizard spells of level 1 or 2 to your spellbook for free. Whenever you gain access to a new spell-slot level in this class, add one eligible Necromancy Wizard spell of a level for which you have spell slots to your spellbook for free. features.name: Ghost Code Archive (Necromancy Spellbook)
features.description: You gain resistance to necrotic damage, and Find Familiar appears in your spellbook. When casting it, you can choose a normal familiar form or the Skeleton or Zombie special form; a normal form can instead have the Undead creature type. When you take the Attack action, you can forgo one of your attacks to let your familiar make one attack using its reaction. When you cast a Necromancy spell using a spell slot, you can choose an Undead creature you can see within 60 feet; it regains hit points equal to the slot level plus your Cyber-Mage level.

choices.name: Choose a familiar form when casting Find Familiar
choices.allowed_options: A normal Find Familiar form, Skeleton, or Zombie; a normal form may have the Undead creature type.
choices.eligibility_rule: Choose when casting Find Familiar; use the supplied special familiar stat blocks for Skeleton and Zombie.
choices.selection_effect: Record the familiar's form and creature type; the choice is made when casting, not permanently at level-up.

levels.notes: Find Familiar is added to the spellbook, not automatically prepared. The supplied source does not resolve whether gaining Savant at the same level as level 2 slots also triggers an additional Savant spell; review before automation.

features.name: Ghost Protocol Deployment (Undead Thralls)
features.description: Animate Dead is always prepared and can be cast once without a spell slot per long rest. Whenever you start casting it, you can increase its effective level by 1. While holding your spellbook, each Undead created or summoned by a Necromancy spell you cast gains maximum and current hit points equal to your Intelligence modifier plus half your Cyber-Mage level, rounded down. Also while holding your spellbook, when an Undead you control within 60 feet hits a creature with an attack roll, it deals extra necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1).

features.name: Ghost Network Mastery (Death's Master)
features.description: While holding your spellbook, you gain both benefits. Bolster Undead: as a bonus action, choose any number of Undead within 60 feet that you created or summoned with a Necromancy spell; each gains temporary hit points equal to your Cyber-Mage level. Use this bonus action once per long rest. Extinguish Undead: when an Undead you can see is reduced to 0 hit points, you can make it explode. Roll a number of d6s equal to half its unexpended Hit Dice, rounded up (minimum 1d6). Each creature in a 10-foot emanation from it makes a Dexterity saving throw; on a failure it takes necrotic damage equal to the roll and cannot take reactions until the start of its next turn, and on a success it takes half damage only. To explode an Undead you do not control, you must also use a reaction and expend a level 5 or higher spell slot.
